title: Electrical Systems and Basic Electronic, Hydraulic and Pneumatic Principles

lessons.title: Electrical principles and tractor circuits
lessons.html:
Voltage, current and resistance

Electricity flows in a closed circuit from the battery positive, through a load such as a lamp, and back to the battery negative, usually through the tractor's metal frame (earth or ground).

  • Voltage (V) is the electrical pressure. Most tractors use 12 V; some large machines use 24 V.
  • Current (A) is the flow of electricity.
  • Resistance (ohm) opposes the flow.

Ohm's law links them: voltage equals current multiplied by resistance (V = I x R). Power in watts equals voltage multiplied by current. A 12 V headlamp drawing 5 A uses 60 W.

Series and parallel

In a series circuit, current flows through each load in turn, so if one fails all stop. Tractor lighting uses parallel circuits, where each load has its own path, so one blown lamp does not switch off the others.

Main tractor circuits

  • Starting: battery, ignition switch, safety (neutral) start switch, starter relay or solenoid, starter motor.
  • Charging: alternator with regulator, warning lamp, battery.
  • Lighting and signalling: head, work, tail, brake and indicator lights, hazard flasher.
  • Instruments and sensors: gauges, warning lamps, sensors for temperature, oil pressure and speed.

Fuses and circuit breakers protect wiring from overload. Always replace a fuse with one of the same rating. A fuse that keeps blowing means a fault to find, not a reason to fit a bigger fuse.

Basic electronics

Modern tractors use electronic components: diodes let current flow one way only, as in the alternator rectifier; transistors act as fast electronic switches; sensors turn temperature, pressure or position into electrical signals; and electronic control units (ECUs) read sensors and control outputs. ECUs on a tractor often talk to each other over a CAN bus network. Protect electronics: disconnect the battery before welding, and never pierce wire insulation with test probes.

Battery safety

Batteries give off explosive hydrogen gas and contain acid. Wear eye protection, no sparks or flames nearby, remove the negative lead first and refit it last.

lessons.title: Hydraulic and pneumatic principles
lessons.html:
Fluid power

Fluid power uses a liquid (hydraulics) or air (pneumatics) under pressure to transmit force. Tractors rely on hydraulics for the three-point linkage, loaders, steering, wet brakes and transmission control. Pneumatics appears in trailer air brakes, seat suspension and some planters' seed metering.

Pascal's principle

Pressure applied to a confined fluid acts equally in all directions. Force equals pressure multiplied by area. A small piston with little force can therefore create pressure that drives a large piston with great force. This is how a hydraulic cylinder lifts a heavy plough.

Basic hydraulic circuit

  1. Reservoir: stores oil, often the transmission housing.
  2. Pump: creates flow. Gear pumps give fixed flow; piston pumps can vary flow on load-sensing systems.
  3. Relief valve: limits maximum pressure to protect the system.
  4. Control valves: direct oil to the right port.
  5. Actuators: cylinders for straight-line movement, motors for rotation.
  6. Filters, hoses and coolers.

A pump makes flow, not pressure. Pressure builds when flow meets resistance from the load.

Pneumatics

A compressor driven by the engine fills an air tank through a dryer and governor. Valves send air to brake chambers or other actuators. Air is compressible, so pneumatic systems are softer than hydraulic ones, but they are clean and leaks are less messy. Drain water from air tanks regularly.

Comparing systems

HydraulicPneumatic
MediumOilAir
ForceVery highModerate
ControlPrecise, stiffSofter, springy

Safety

Hydraulic oil under pressure can be injected through skin by a pinhole leak and cause serious injury that needs urgent medical help. Never feel for leaks with your hand; use cardboard. Lower implements and release pressure before disconnecting hoses. Never stand under raised loads held only by hydraulics.

Key points

  • V = I x R links voltage, current and resistance.
  • Replace fuses with the same rating and find the fault.
  • Disconnect the battery before welding to protect ECUs.
  • Force equals pressure times area; pumps make flow, load makes pressure.
  • Never check hydraulic leaks by hand and release pressure before disconnecting.
